verdict.rationale: Semgrep's docs describe writing custom rules in its pattern-based syntax, testing them in the Semgrep Editor, and using them via CLI/CI to scan repositories; community evidence confirms security engineers use custom rules to catch codebase-specific antipatterns. Rules are stored as YAML config files that can be version-controlled and shared/reused across repos via registry or CI config. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation/demo of a central rule-sharing mechanism (e.g., private rule registry workflow) beyond general CI/config references.
